sanskrit_verse: अभिगन्तास्मि भगिनीं मातरं वा तवेति ह / शपन्तं दापयेद् राजा पञ्चविंशतिकं दमम् //
transliteration: abhi-gantāsmi bhaginīṁ mātaraṁ vā taveiti ha / śapantaṁ dāpayed rājā pañca-viṁśatikaṁ damam //
sph_interpretive_translation: One who falsely claims another's sister or mother as their own shall be made by the king to pay a fine of twenty-five units, upon taking an oath.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the sovereign to enforce restorative justice
Causation arises through false assertion disrupting familial integrity
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by intentional misrepresentation
Restoration logic demands compensation proportional to violation
Consciousness alignment requires purification of relational truth
executable_legal_axioms: IF claimant asserts ownership over another's kin without factual basis THEN impose compensatory fine of twenty-five units
IF false kinship claim disrupts social harmony THEN require oath-taking for karmic accountability
IF claimant lacks capacity for truthful discernment THEN initiate consciousness-realignment protocol post-adjudication
IF violation occurs THEN ensure victim receives full restitution prior to societal reintegration of offender
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this verse establishes that any individual asserting false familial claims must undergo judicial scrutiny and financial restitution. The court must ensure the claimant takes a formal oath, affirming the gravity of conscious misalignment. Responsibility is tied not to intent alone but to disruption caused within the relational fabric upheld by Dharma.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: This provision aligns with Nyaya through pramana-based adjudication—verifiable truth supersedes false assertion. It reflects anupurvasah: untruth manifests sequentially as disharmony, necessitating corrective action. Responsibility is proportional; no punitive suffering is mandated. Instead, restoration flows via conscious completion and lawful correction.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Oath-administration protocol to restore personal integrity
Compensatory transfer to affected party for energetic balance
Completion process ensuring cessation of false assertions publicly
Reintegration support for offender post-financial settlement
final_declaration: By the Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Source of all Dharma, this law stands executed—not for punishment, but for the realignment of consciousness, the restoration of relational truth, and the reaffirmation of Sanatana Dharma's supremacy in governance.
